summary: Polish private foundry (210 staff, EUR 9.8 M) under restructuring, bank watching monthly; we are 7 % of its turnover. Poor quality: red scorecard, OTD 63.5 %, 2376 ppm, 38 complaints, escalation letter sent. It owns the tooling; Bearing bracket HN has 70190 qualified, HN 200 runs 30/70 with 70120. It holds price (kept 91 % of asks) and moves in small ~EUR 0.50 steps; faster payment and paying overdue invoices are what buy price.
notes: Needs cash: bank pressure, restructuring, repeated 10-day payment requests; resents our late payments (8.8 days avg, 76 % over 5 days). Fears margin loss. 3 open 8D (letter: none overdue). Trades a ppm commitment for a higher price.
fears: chargebacks and losing the bearing bracket to 70190

levers: payment in 10-14 days written into the deal
binding volume with official volume figures
arguments: quality record: red scorecard, OTD 63.5 %, 2376 ppm, escalation letter
qualified second source 70190 for the bearing bracket
avoid: promising to pay on time without written faster terms
asking for a margin cut without cash in return
changing terms after its final offer
demanding a tight ppm target for free (it prices extra checks)
tactics: Offer written 10-14 day payment terms early; it says that helps more than anything.
Lead with the red scorecard and escalation letter; ask for a binding improvement plan.
Commit a binding volume and send the volume figures when asked.
Expect EUR 0.50 steps; keep moving visibly each round or it freezes.
Do not let it price a ppm commitment up; tie ppm to the chargeback clause instead.
playbook.expected_concession: Arena P11 (7 deals, 0 walked): opened 47.0, R1 held or 46.5, then ~0.50 steps to 46.0-46.5 by R3-5 (one deal at 46.1; one held 47.0 with a 300 EUR chargeback); final offer median R5; best score 0.63.
